blogs.title: Beyond the Stomach: When GLP-1 Agonists Trigger Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy
blogs.description: This post explores the emerging, albeit rare, association between GLP-1 receptor agonists (like semaglutide) and immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM). We contrast the classic timeline of direct toxic rhabdomyolysis—which resolves quickly upon drug cessation—with the delayed, progressive, and severe autoimmune phenotype seen in this case. The discussion highlights why clinicians must distinguish between simple muscle wasting or toxicity and a true autoimmune process requiring immunosuppression.

blogs.title: Seronegative IMNM: Navigating Diagnosis When Autoantibodies Are Missing
blogs.description: Focusing on the diagnostic challenge presented by this case, this article examines the implications of a 'seronegative' IMNM diagnosis. With standard panels for anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP returning negative, we discuss the limitations of current testing, the significance of muscle biopsy findings (necrosis with minimal lymphocytic infiltrate), and how to manage patients when classic biomarkers are absent. We also touch on the unexpected finding of isolated SS-B positivity and its potential relevance.

blogs.title: The Statin Parallel: What Semaglutide Teaches Us About Drug-Induced Autoimmunity
blogs.description: Drawing a historical parallel to statin-associated autoimmune myopathy (SAAM), this post analyzes how drug exposure can act as a trigger for persistent autoimmunity even after the offending agent is withdrawn. Unlike typical drug-induced myalgia or acute rhabdomyolysis, this case illustrates a phenomenon where the immune system continues to attack muscle tissue long after clearance of the drug, necessitating a paradigm shift in monitoring patients on new metabolic therapies.

blogs.title: Red Flags in Metabolic Therapy: Distinguishing Dysphagia from Deconditioning in Obese Patients
blogs.description: This clinical pearl focuses on recognizing early warning signs in patients starting weight-loss medications. We analyze how progressive dysphagia and dysphonia—often dismissed as deconditioning or unrelated GI issues—can be harbingers of bulbar involvement in necrotizing myopathy. The post provides a checklist for emergency physicians and primary care providers evaluating obese patients presenting with unexplained weakness or swallowing difficulties after initiating GLP-1 therapy.

blogs.title: Therapeutic Triage: Why This Patient Needed IVIG When Others Might Not
blogs.description: A deep dive into management strategies for severe drug-triggered IMNM. Unlike uncomplicated rhabdomyolysis managed with fluids, or mild steroid-responsive myopathies, this case required aggressive dual-modality therapy (high-dose steroids plus IVIG) to halt progression. We review the decision-making process for escalating immunosuppression in seronegative cases and discuss the prognosis regarding weaning protocols based on this patient's rapid recovery compared to idiopathic IMNM.
